intro: California holds the biggest living things on earth and some of its most photographed trees, and they are rarely the same trees. The giant sequoias stand in the Sierra, where General Sherman was wrapped in foil in 2021 while the fire burned toward it. The coast redwoods stand in fog along the Russian River, a short walk from a car park at Armstrong Woods. Palo Alto is named for a single redwood that still stands beside the railway. The cities have their own kind of old tree: Moreton Bay figs planted by Victorian gardeners across Los Angeles and San Diego, Monterey cypresses bent by the wind at Point Lobos, and a numbered Landmark Tree list in San Francisco that protects a cork oak on 20th Street.
